title: Clinical efficacy of 0.01% atropine in retarding the progression of myopia in children

groups.description: single-vision spectacles only (S group), randomised against SA; Dalian, China
spectacles plus 0.01% atropine once nightly in both eyes (SA group)
orthokeratology lenses only (OK group); children who had worn ortho-K lenses for 3 months, randomised against OKA
orthokeratology plus 0.01% atropine once nightly (lenses inserted 10 minutes after the drops) (OKA group)

series.notes: mean (SD); Tab1 rows labelled 'Change at 3/6/12 mo' tabulate the axial length at those visits and the 'Change over 3/6/12 mo' rows the change from baseline, so the absolute series is used; the study included both eyes (160 eyes of 80 children) and the table gives n = 20 children per group, used as tabulated; no dropouts reported

exclusions.what: Tab1 AL 'Change over 3/6/12 mo' rows (change from baseline)
exclusions.reason: the same table gives the absolute axial length; the absolute series is used (protocol: Values)

exclusions.what: Tab1 SE, Schirmer's test and TBuT rows; Tab2 and Tab3 (Schirmer's test, TBuT)

notes: 80 children aged 5–14 years with myopia (cycloplegic SE at least −1.00 D, sphere −1.00 to −6.00 DS), Second Affiliated Hospital of Dalian Medical University, January 2019 to April 2020: 40 randomised to spectacles (S) or spectacles plus 0.01% atropine (SA); 40 who had worn ortho-K lenses for 3 months randomised to ortho-K (OK) or ortho-K plus 0.01% atropine (OKA).
AL by an LS 900 biometer (Lenstar), mean of five measurements; units mm (Tab1); visits every 3 months, AL tabulated at 3, 6 and 12 months.

Methods state that patients ceased wearing ortho-K lenses and were examined weekly until corneal curvature regressed and refraction stabilised 'during the follow-up visit' (a refraction procedure); its timing relative to the AL measurements is not stated.
Spherical equivalent, Schirmer's test and tear break-up time are tabulated and not used.
